commitMessages: c239dd3 修复工具失败恢复与负责人补齐分片后的交付结算（KEJ-111）
baselineProof: Every old covered source/fixture/dependency was independently git-show compared against its stored SHA256 at 49d2bc0; all match. This establishes an exact available old-source baseline, without relabeling prior runs.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Adds requiredSourceIds checking and synthetic per-partition recovery criteria. Authority and LocalEffects finite graph drivers never submit checks. HostRetry submits its original short candidate without partitionRecoveries or any discussion. LocalEffects concrete process bridges do complete an answer/check pair, and SQLite report bridges submit a candidate; all lack discussion/claims. Thus mapRecoveryCriteria returns [] and existing requirements retain their original diagnostic rules.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Recovery-bearing candidates now force full check materials. The four finite graph drivers do not execute the independent-check runner. LocalEffects actual process bridges do execute one deterministic check, without a recovery claim or previous check; this new conditional is false. No permit, local effect or retry-batch transition is changed.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Extends a TypeScript union of model output fields with partitionRecoveries; no runtime transition, identity or measurement/accounting statement changes.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Adds known-settled Web failure feedback, saved recovery context, validated recovery output and owner/check prompt instructions. The four finite graph drivers invoke TeamEngine/LocalRuntime/CliJournal directly and never OpenAICompatibleAdapter or model HTTP. LocalEffects additionally runs three concrete process bridges through WebService/WorkRunner/real Adapter with an injected deterministic transport returning only answer/check; those cases have no Web output, no discussion and no partitionRecoveries. Thus the new Web loop is outside these graph action alphabets and dormant in the retained bridge requests. Its safety is separately checked by ToolRecovery plus concrete BDD, not inferred from these old graphs.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Adds recordToolFailure callback bound to the last authorized Web request, plus validation/projection of optional partitionRecoveries. The finite graph drivers do not instantiate WorkRunner; LocalRuntime binding calls the runtime directly and stops at the launch callback. LocalEffects process bridges run WorkRunner but their deterministic transport emits only answer/check without recovery claims and never authorizes Web requests, so the callback is not invoked. Existing beginExecution/LOCAL_* paths are unchanged.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: The submission gate calls mapRecoveryProblem, which immediately returns null when claims are absent. Check-result recovery is conditional on a recovery-bearing candidate and a delivered current map round; no such state is reachable in these drivers. HostRetry retains its original candidate and never checks it; authority late-DELIVER probes remain stale and rejected.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Adds a root RECORD_TOOL_FAILURE valid/apply-or-reject handler. None of these four models/drivers emits that event. Existing ordered always retirement/start, RECOVER, STOP and LOCAL_* handlers are unchanged, so old action-to-transaction correspondence is retained.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: New transitive dependency: pure validation and criteria projection plus resolution writes only after a successful bound recovery check. These drivers have no map discussion; no claim is submitted. Thus new validation/criteria return their empty legacy result and resolveMapRecoveries cannot write a partition resolution or clear incomplete in this finite domain. Hash capture is a drift gate, not proof of recovery semantics.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Existing LOCAL_* dispatch still returns localEventProblem first. Added DELIVER structural validation accepts omitted claims and the new switch case runs only for RECORD_TOOL_FAILURE; all prior permit, fence, session, approval and request guards for these driver events are unchanged.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Optional recovery claims are copied on DELIVER only when present; resolveMapRecoveries executes only on successful CHECK_RESULT and returns before writes when no current delivered map round/claims exist; recordToolFailure executes only for the new event. These four finite graph alphabets never reach new writes. LocalEffects process bridge answer/check and report DELIVER omit claims/discussion, so the new calls preserve legacy behavior. HostRetry DELIVER omits claims and asserts complete candidate equality throughout replay.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: New transitive dependency: guards and bounded append of intent.toolRecovery.failures for RECORD_TOOL_FAILURE. It neither modifies local operations/checkpoints/leases nor grants approval or permits. The event is absent from these four graphs; budget and stale-failure combinations are independently modeled by ToolRecovery, not folded into these older domains.

reviewedChanges.classification: no effect on the declared finite slice
reviewedChanges.reason: Adds optional recovery facts and event/output contracts without changing existing execution tickets, local session/approval identity, local operation status or Store semantics. No default recovery data is inserted into existing intents/candidates.

verification: Every assigned full entrypoint passed on frozen c239 product bytes, including existing model/source negative controls, restored model/code replay, fresh independent reader and applicable reader fault controls. Covered sources stayed unchanged. No real product bug found by these old finite slices.
limitations: No proof of model decision quality, external HTTP/provider liveness, arbitrary Web feedback combined with host operations, arbitrary map recovery combined with host effects, infinite failures or OS/hardware correctness. New dependency hashes alone do not extend old model guarantees.
syncPolicy: Parent centrally reviews and updates candidate pins. syncCommit stays old until all nine complete frozen-source CI entrypoints and independent evidence readers pass. No prior-source proof is transplanted.
concreteBridgeScope: Three controlled CLI/SIGKILL cases exercise real WebService/WorkRunner/OpenAICompatibleAdapter with injected deterministic transport, not a real model supplier; answer/check only, no Web requests, map discussion or recovery claims. Four SQLite commit-boundary cases use direct TeamEngine events, including ordinary report DELIVER without claims. This distinction prevents the finite graph no-Adapter limit being incorrectly generalized to all bridge execution.
verificationChanges: Correspondence review and conservative transitive dependency fingerprints only; no model, property, domain, fairness, driver or control weakened or changed.
